findings.where: Motion sketch (the timeline table and 'Replay the note'), and the hero it describes, at both widths
findings.fault: The only thing that moves on the page is the call to action writing itself in. So the first moment that catches the eye is the page asking for something. The brief asks for the opposite: a calm moment before any text asks for anything. It also asks for smooth animation built around the aqueduct. The aqueduct sketch, the one drawing that could carry that moment, stays still. This tile sets the motion principles for the animation round, and it points that round towards animating the ask rather than the aqueduct.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who wants calm first and dislikes anything pushy or busy. The founder, whose LoveFrom ruling limits the motion idea to smooth animation built around the aqueduct. The animation round (#9) would inherit a principle that goes against both.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.' under the subhead (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The first screen spends its third line on a claim of size, 'over 40 years', instead of something a reader can check. The line before it already gives a checkable credential: former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group. The italic line then adds a boast that a procurement reader discounts, and it pushes the tone towards the firm voice the brand sheet rejects.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staff member choosing a consultant against terms of reference: they look for named bodies, roles and regions, not years in total. Mark's own brief also objects: confident, one strong line, no boasts.

findings.where: Nav bar (the gummed binding), the logo at top left, at both widths
findings.fault: The logo is shrunk to a small cream line drawing and 'MMM INFRA' set in the page's own serif. The logo's blue wordmark and its descriptor 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' are gone. Next to the much larger headline and the aqueduct sketch, the brand mark is the weakest thing on the first screen. A visitor who knows MMM Infra from Mark's LinkedIn or current site would not recognise it.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief says the logo stays and whose animation ideas end on the full logo. A returning visitor would wonder whether this is the same practice.

findings.where: Article specimen, the heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop)
findings.fault: On desktop the heading's two lines sit two rules apart, with as much space between them as between separate blocks. They read as two headings, or as a heading and a stray line, not as one title. On the phone the same heading is set tight and reads as one. The tile's article specimen, the one place the layout round takes its heading form from, therefore gives two different answers.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page, who at first sees two titles. The designers of the layout round, who cannot tell which spacing is meant.

findings.where: Palette, the swatch grid (Pad, Under-sheet, Feint, Margin red / Ballpoint, Light hand, Binding), at both widths
findings.fault: Each swatch's three label lines (name, hex, role) drop down the ruled lines. The last line, 'ground' or 'the stack', ends up about as close to the next row's swatch as the name is to its own swatch. So by proximity the role words group with the wrong colour as easily as with the right one.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or the next round's designer, reading which colour does which job: misreading 'ground' as belonging to Ballpoint means using the wrong colour.
